note: The ketiv is 'ovrenu "we crossed", the qere 'ovram "they crossed"; KJV follows the ketiv (as if the narrator were an eyewitness), I follow the qere.
Charvot tsurim are knives of flint (tsur "rock, flint"), a detail of the archaic rite that "sharp" obscures.
Giv'at ha-'aralot is treated as a place name; KJV translates it, which is accurate in sense.

kjv: the old corn of the land
note: 'Avur (only here and v.12) means produce or yield of the land; "old corn" is a guess from the context of eating before the new harvest, and "corn" now suggests maize.
